title: Patterns over log lines

blocks.md:
## A pattern is a tiny parser

A log line looks like `[WARN]   beacon   down`. You want the level and the message, without the noise.

- `/\s+/` means one or more whitespace characters.
- `^` and `$` anchor the pattern to the start and end of the line.
- Parentheses **capture**: `/^\[(\w+)\]\s*(.*)$/` keeps the level in group 1 and the rest in group 2.
- `exec` returns `null` when nothing matched, or an array whose slots 1 and 2 are those groups.

`"a  b  c".replace(/\s+/, " ")` fixes only the **first** run of spaces. Add the `g` flag — `/\s+/g` — to fix every run. That missing `g` is the bug people ship most.

Regex is for lines and fields. It is the wrong tool for HTML; you already have a document tree for that.

choices.md: `a-b  c` — only the first run changed

blocks.promptMd: In `/^\[(\w+)\]\s*(.*)$/`, the parentheses {{a}} that part of the match, and `^` {{b}}.
blocks.explainMd: Groups come back as slots 1, 2, … on the exec result. Anchors stop the pattern from matching in the middle of a longer line.

blocks.promptMd: `exec` throws when the line does not match the pattern.
blocks.explainMd: It returns null. Check for null before reading the capture groups, or you will read a property of null.

blocks.promptMd: > `tidy(line)` turns `"[WARN]   beacon   down  "` into `"warn: beacon down"`. A line with no `[LEVEL]` tag gets the level `info`. Print `tidy("[WARN]   beacon   down  ")`.

hintLadder.md: Two jobs: pull the level out of the brackets, and squeeze the runs of spaces in the message.
`/^\[(\w+)\]\s*(.*)$/.exec(line)` gives you the level and the rest, or `null` when there is no tag.
Collapse spacing with the global flag: `text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim()`.

description: A pattern pulls fields out of a log line and squeezes the spacing. Without the global flag it fixes only the first match.
